passages.note: House final-passage vote, Yea; 6 Nays of 65 voting (under 10%), so it cannot carry a chair alone.

passages.provision_quote: (3) Notwithstanding any other provision of law, a school or LEA may not: 45 (a) prohibit a parent of a child from accessing the child's education record; or 46 (b) without written parental consent make changes to a student's education record 47 regarding a student's gender identity that does not conform with the student's sex.
passages.note: Guarantees parental access to records and requires consent for gender-identity record changes; it neither requires proactive notification (rung 4) nor consent before staff use a name or pronouns (rung 5), and goes beyond on-request access alone (rung 3), so it shows only the parent-side direction.

rows.reasoning: Christofferson voted Yea on S.B. 100 (2023), which bars a school from prohibiting a parent's access to the child's education record and from changing that record's gender identity entry "without written parental consent". That places him on the parent-information side, but the bill does not match every clause of one rung: it does not "Require schools to notify parents", it does not require "parental permission before staff use a different name or pronouns", and its consent clause goes beyond "tell parents when parents ask"; the vote is also near-unanimous (6 Nays).
